deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page, so there is nothing to reconstruct mathematically. The page is a heavily abbreviated, partly shorthand German prose draft on German historiography (Geschichtschreibung).

Layout as far as it can be read:
- Heading: 'Erster Hauptteil.'
- Subheading: 'Die deutsche Geschichtschreibung [seit/während ... ]' – the end of the line is not securely legible.
- Chapter title: 'Kap. I. d[ie] deutsche Geschichte u[nd] d[ie] Gegenwart' (or similar).

First paragraph: it seems to list three requirements of historical writing: 1. the material (Stoff); 2. the conception or apprehension of the material (Auffassung des Stoffs); 3. the artistic treatment (künstlerische Behandlung). It then discusses the first requirement, the material. It argues that a complete, many-sided presentation (allseitige Darstellung) of German history requires considering the present as well, not only past history.

Second paragraph: it treats the late emergence of a consciousness of the German nation, set against particularism (Partikularismus). It refers to:
- city histories (Stadtgeschichte);
- the treatment of 'Kaiser und Reich' as merely 'historisch';
- histories of the smaller states, with names such as Bayern and possibly Sachsen in parenthesis;
- histories of the larger states, apparently naming Württemberg among others.

Context:
- The previous page is rhetorical prose about the life of nature and the striving of the researcher's mind (Forschergeist).
- The next page begins a piece titled 'Methode', on two activities of the mind in finding a proof: critical verification of each step versus a reproductive and productive grasp of the whole.

This page therefore belongs to non-mathematical essay or lecture material. Both the hand and the topic, a planned treatise on German historiography, make it doubtful that it is a Riemann composition. It may be an excerpt, a draft by another person, or a Gymnasium or student exercise kept in the 'Varia' bundle. Attribution should be treated as uncertain.

transcription_corrections: The body is not entirely 'illegible shorthand'. It is abbreviated German longhand (Kurrent with heavy contractions).
Line 1 of the body most likely reads, in substance: the requirements of the writing of history are three (... 1, der Stoff; 2, die Auffassung des Stoffs; 3, die künstlerische Behandlung).
'Particularismus' / 'Partikularismus' and 'Stadtgeschichte' appear to be read correctly. A parenthesis naming states (Bayern, possibly Sachsen) refers to the 'kleinen Staaten'.
The chapter title is plausibly 'Kap. I. Die deutsche Geschichte und die Gegenwart'.
The faint mirror-image text in the upper half is bleed-through from the verso. It is not part of this page's text.
